name: KeyBelt
notes: One-step install and automatic updates: drag drag_n_drop.py into Maya and KeyBelt installs itself to Documents/maya/KeyBelt (shared by every Maya version). Settings > General > Updates checks for new versions in the background; nothing is downloaded until you click Download update, and the update is applied the next time Maya starts. KeyBelt now ships as a compiled, protected build under a free-to-use license (EULA.txt).

Maya preference helpers: asset-centric selection and Maya's cycle check warnings are turned off at every launch (Settings > General > Maya Preferences, on by default). Unticking restores your previous Maya values.

Time Dragger HUD: hold the Time Dragger key and drag (LMB / MMB) for an endless scrub with a temporary timeline showing the range, keys of the selection and bookmarks. Shift = fine, Ctrl = coarse, wheel = one frame, Esc = cancel. Toggle in Settings > General > Time Dragger (off = Maya's own Time Dragger). Only a key still bound to Maya's Time Dragger is rerouted.

Settings window reorganised: General / Toolbars / Hotkeys / Radial & Viewport Bar / Documentation. Timeline Tools and Graph Editor are merged into Toolbars (one action-button list with timeline + Graph Editor columns); Quick Access is now Radial & Viewport Bar with one shared tool palette. General uses cards (Toolbar, Keys Sliders, Time Dragger, Startup, Session).
The Radial Menu tool palette no longer lists the Settings tool itself.
Graph Editor toolbar sliders now stretch to the free width (48–240 px each) and the toolbar never forces the Graph Editor to stay wide: when it's too narrow, it is cut off at the right edge.
